The biodegradability and reduced environmental risk of synthetic and natural ester fluids are particularly important for hydropower plants located near sensitive water bodies (Malde, Coker, and Tuck 2024). In 1979, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Toxic Substances Control Act banned the use of polychlorinated biphenyls, or PCBs, in cooling oil, making them more environmentally suitable as well. 1.3 Current State of the LPT Supply Chain The current state of the LPT supply chain for the U.S. hydropower sector is defined by an aging fleet of transformers operating beyond their average service life, limited domestic manufacturing and assembly capacity, extended procurement lead times, and a heavy reliance on imports for both finished units and critical raw material inputs. The total number of LPTs in the United States was estimated to be between 4,900 and 6,799 in 2022. While this total is increasing with the addition of more than 700 LPTs each year, approximately 170 LPTs reach their design lifetime annually, emphasizing the growing need for replacement alongside new installations (Nguyen et al. 2022). In 2019, the U.S. Department of Commerce found that 82% of LPTs (617 units) were imported for domestic usage, and only 18% were domestically produced (Bureau of Industry and Security 2021). As of 2023, U.S. manufacturers were meeting approximately 30% of domestic demand for LPTs (USITC 2024a). U.S. demand and manufacturing of LPTs are shown in Figure 2. Manufacturers have a limited number of production slots to make various transformer types, including LPTs. The facilities listed in Table 1 can produce transformers rated at or above 100 MVA, although they may also produce smaller transformers. Although the share of domestic production has increased, domestic manufacturing capability has not expanded to match the increase in demand. Between 2011 and 2023, apparent consumption of LPTs in the United States increased by 28% while manufacturing capacity increased by 11%. During this period, domestic manufacturers were able to ramp up production from existing facilities, increasing capacity utilization from 40% to 78% (USITC 2024a). Further increases in annual production would likely require additional manufacturing capacity. Since 2023, domestic LPT producers Delta Star and Hitachi Energy USA have expanded their manufacturing facilities (both in Virginia), and Pennsylvania Transformer announced an expansion of its facility in North Carolina (Hitachi Energy 2022; Delta Star Inc. 2025; North Carolina Office of the Governor 2025). Siemens Energy announced that it is building a new production facility in Charlotte, North Carolina, which is expected to begin operations in 2027 (Delaloye 2024).
